description: The bookkeeping that stops the checklist becoming a survey. These gates answer to the run's own state rather than to an attestation, so a run cannot close by saying it is finished.

gates.title: The Run Was Opened Before The Work
gates.rule: A run exists and the changes are recorded against it. A schema change made outside a run is a change nothing compared against the code, and afterwards it looks exactly like one that was checked.

gates.title: The Database Was Read, Not Reasoned About
gates.rule: The schema came from a query against the live database in this run. Migrations describe what was intended; only the catalogue says what is there. A table created by hand, an index dropped in the dashboard, and a policy edited in the console are all invisible to a repository read.

gates.title: Every Table Was Ruled On
gates.rule: Each table in the probe ends either kept with its reader named, or removed. A table nobody looked at and a table considered and kept are indistinguishable without this, and the second is the whole point of the run.
gates.fix: db-pass.py tables, then for each one either drop it or table-clear it naming what reads it.

gates.title: Nothing Was Dropped Without A Backup
gates.rule: Every table this run removes was exported first and the run records where the export went. A drop is the one action here with no undo, and a restore nobody can find is the same as no backup at all.
gates.fix: Export the rows, then db-pass.py backup --path <where> --tables <names>, or answer n/a when the run dropped nothing.

gates.title: What Belongs To Another Checklist Was Handed Over
gates.rule: This checklist asks whether the database and the code agree, and nothing else. Whether a service answers belongs to the stack checklist, how long a page takes to the performance checklist. Each is named and handed over, never resolved here and never dropped.
gates.fix: db-pass.py delegate --to <stack|perf|design|seo> --note "<what was found>", or answer n/a when nothing outside this checklist came up.

gates.title: Every Applicable Gate Is Answered
gates.rule: No gate is left silent. A gate that is not met is work to do; the only ways past one are changing the database or the code, or naming the condition that puts it out of scope.
gates.fix: db-pass.py status lists what is open.

gates.title: The Filled Checklist Was Rendered
gates.rule: The run ends with the whole checklist shown - every gate, its verdict, the evidence, what was delegated, and a section listing anything answered not applicable and why.
